Make each lake's flowpaths a contiguous subgraph

Source: R/repairs.R
close_lake_id_gaps.Rd

t-route collapses every flowpath sharing a lake_id into one waterbody node. That is only valid if those flowpaths are connected: a non-member sitting between two members turns lake -> gap -> lake into node_L -> gap -> node_L, a cycle, and routing with waterbodies enabled fails on it.

Membership is a length-weighted majority of a flowpath's member reaches, a rule that decides each flowpath alone and cannot see the network: a reach mostly outside the lake is rejected even when both its neighbours are members. An earlier closure runs before divide-less leaf flowpaths are demoted, which rewires flowpath_toid and can open a gap that was not there before, so this runs once the topology is final.

It only ever adds a lake_id to a flowpath already bracketed by one lake, so it cannot change a fabric with no gaps and cannot move a flowpath between lakes.

The stamp is propagated to flowlines and network, which inherit lake_id from their flowpath and would otherwise disagree with it.

Usage

close_lake_id_gaps(
  input_gpkg,
  max_step = 5L,
  flowpath_layer = "flowpaths",
  nexus_layer = "nexus",
  flowline_layer = "flowlines",
  network_layer = "network"
)

Arguments

input_gpkg

Path to the NextGen GeoPackage.

max_step

Longest run of non-members to bridge. Beyond this the gap is a genuine river between two arms of one waterbody and is left to be reported rather than silently absorbed.

flowpath_layer, nexus_layer, flowline_layer, network_layer

Layer names.

Value

Invisibly, a character vector of the flowpath_ids stamped.
